_status: Candidates, 2026-11-20. NOTHING has been taken from any of them. Each is listed with the fields it could actually fill, because breadth is not the question - the question is which column a source can fill and whether we may redistribute it.
_redistribution: The care needed here is about REDISTRIBUTION, not about looking things up. Reading a public page and recording that a given converter uses a given chip is using a fact, and facts are not protectable. Copying a compiled list wholesale into this catalogue and then passing that catalogue on is a different act, and a compiled database can be protected in its own right - the European sui generis database right would apply. So: take facts per device with the source recorded, which is what every record here already does, rather than importing a list in bulk. Whether this catalogue is ever published, and under what terms, is not decided and is the author's call alone.
_the_field_none_of_them_has: None of these carries dsd_reconverted_to_pcm or dsd_direct - the two fields that decide whether Auto sends DSD at all. They come from measurement or from a documented statement about that device, and nothing else. So these sources can carry the catalogue from level 0 to level 1 at scale, and to a PARTIAL level 2. Never to a complete one.

candidates.name: DutchAudioClassics, complete D/A converter list
candidates._value: Highest of the four. The converter chip per model is the field that carries the whole cascade, and with it per model we barely need brand-level inference.
candidates._caveat: Skewed to CD players and vintage converters, many with no USB input at all, so they can never be identified automatically and most cannot receive upsampled PCM over USB.

candidates.name: CD-Player-DAC-Transport list
candidates._value: Same column as above, useful as a cross-check: two independent lists agreeing on a chip is worth more than either alone.

candidates.name: NativeDSD device database
candidates._value: 600+ converters, players and portables, filterable by DSD rate. Three fields on modern hardware, which is the hardware our listeners own.
candidates._caveat: A commercial shop's own compilation. Licence to be settled first.

candidates.name: Audio Science Review, measurement index
candidates._value: A different axis from the others: measured behaviour rather than parts. The only listed source that could ever support correctable, and the one that could tell us a ladder's real depth rather than its interface's.
candidates._caveat: Per-thread prose, not a table. Reading it is work per device, not a harvest.

candidates.name: Gearspace, audio interfaces and their AD/DA chips
candidates._value: Narrow: studio interfaces. Relevant because several of them are what a listener actually has on the end of a zone.
